definition: Cognitive functioning refers to how well a person’s mental abilities are working in ways that affect learning, participation in treatment, and day-to-day recovery. In psychiatric settings, it can be measured through cognitive or neuropsychological assessment and may influence clinical planning.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define cognitive functioning as “how well a person’s mental abilities are working,” so this framing is not directly supported.

The packet supports that cognitive functioning relates to “treatment engagement, learning, and functional recovery,” but it does not explicitly mention “participation in treatment” or “day-to-day recovery” as stated.

The packet says cognitive and neuropsychological functioning “have been assessed,” but it does not specify that in psychiatric settings cognitive functioning “can be measured through cognitive or neuropsychological assessment,” nor does it provide details establishing this as the measurement mechanism.

While the packet states cognitive functioning is underutilized and insufficiently integrated into treatment planning, it does not specifically support the claim that it “may influence clinical planning” in the broad sense used in the definition.
